problems.stem: You are publishing your workflow write-up as a GitHub Pages site. What must the repo root homepage be named so the site URL works?
problems.explanation: GitHub Pages serves index.html as the default page at the site root. Another name leaves the root URL showing a 404.

problems.stem: Your live page shows a broken image. The tag reads . What is the correct fix?
options: Use a repository-relative path like and commit the image into the repo
Switch the image to a PDF
Add the image again to the same folder on your desktop
problems.explanation: A C:/Users path only resolves on your own machine. A relative path to a file inside the repo works for every visitor.

problems.stem: You pushed index.html to the main branch but the site still does not load. What is the most likely missing step?
options: The file needs to be renamed to readme.html
In Settings > Pages, the source branch and folder were never selected, so Pages is not publishing
You must push the file a second time
problems.explanation: Pushing files does not enable publishing on its own. Pages must have a source branch and folder set in Settings.

problems.stem: Your list of workflow steps renders as one run-on line. The HTML is <ul><li>Log time<li>Find slow step<li>Fix it. What is wrong?
options: Lists are not allowed in HTML

The
  • items and the
      are not closed; each item needs and the list needs
You need to use a table instead
problems.explanation: Unclosed and mis-nested tags break the layout. Closing each <li> and the <ul> renders a proper bulleted list.
